sources.name: ui
sources.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: production bitmap UI skin atlas for an original 2D pixel sandbox game "Starsoil"; this is an actual sliced texture asset, not a screenshot.
Primary request: Design a refined, richly shaded pixel-art RPG UI kit with the readability and crafted material feel of Terraria, but completely original shapes and ornaments. Muted midnight indigo enamel, aged copper and warm gold fine borders, restrained turquoise accents, tiny corner rivets and crystal motifs. Compact and elegant rather than heavy.
Composition: One square atlas, exactly 3 columns by 3 rows of equal square tiles with NO gutters, NO margins, NO labels and NO text. The whole canvas is logically 96x96 pixels, each tile exactly 32x32 logical pixels. Render enlarged 16x with nearest-neighbor hard square pixels (1536x1536 output). Do not add tiny detail below the logical pixel grid.
Tiles in row-major order:
1: main window panel, dark blue-grey quiet flat center, fine copper beveled outline and tiny ornate corners.
2: normal button, dark indigo slightly raised, clean light upper edge.
3: selected/pressed button, rich dark teal with copper-gold perimeter.
4: inventory slot, very dark recessed center and subtle steel-copper inset edges.
5: selected inventory slot, same recessed center with a distinct warm gold selected rim.
6: inactive tab, dark recessed blue, understated beveled edge.
7: active tab, slightly brighter teal-blue with gold upper edge.
8: health/mana meter frame, dark hollow recessed inner area with polished copper outer frame.
9: dialogue/recipe card, blue slate center with delicate copper corner braces.
Constraints: Each tile designed for nine-slice use: all four corners fit within 4x4 logical pixels; edge decoration confined to the OUTERMOST 3 pixels; 24x24 central field flat and unobstructed so text and icons fit. Horizontal/vertical edge middle sections must tile seamlessly. Every edge meets its own corner correctly. Tiles align exactly on the 3x3 grid. Fully opaque tile interiors; genuine transparency only outside the tiny clipped outer corners. 20-32 colors shared across atlas, no dithering inside text fields. Crisp square pixel clusters, one-pixel stepped bevels.
Avoid: typography, mockup menus, item icons, invented labels, logos, drop shadows outside tile bounds, blurred edges, anti-aliasing, painterly detail, perspective, excessive filigree.

sources.name: dew-slime
sources.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story
Asset type: production transparent pixel-art enemy animation sprite sheet for the original side-view 2D sandbox Starsoil.
Format is critical: SIX frames, arranged EXACTLY THREE COLUMNS by TWO ROWS, equally sized cells, with no gutters, no margins and no labels. Canvas logical size 96x64 pixels, each cell 32x32 pixels. Each frame contains ONE sprite confined to a centered 24x24 pixel box, logical local coordinates x=4..27 and y=4..27. Draw in a true 24x24 native pixel vocabulary, enlarged exactly 16x with nearest-neighbor hard square edges. Output 1536x1024. Genuine transparent background, including all cell padding. One-pixel dark outline, clean readable silhouette, 12-15 consistent colors shared across all six frames. Single side view facing RIGHT in every frame, same character, fixed scale and proportions; body center x=16; grounded creatures have the feet baseline y=27. No camera motion, no zoom and no frame-specific recentering. Loop order is left-to-right top row frames 1,2,3 then left-to-right bottom row frames 4,5,6, returning smoothly to frame1.
Style: polished, expressive classic pixel sandbox monster with the readability and charm of Terraria, but original creature design for Starsoil, purposeful pixel clusters, warm rim highlights and cool shadows, no copying game assets.
Avoid: text, grid lines, numbered frames, outlines around cells, extra characters, scenery, shadow blobs, gradients, glow outside sprite, blur, antialiasing, isometric view, painterly rendering, smooth vector curves.
Subject and animation: Leaf-dew slime: a translucent jade and mint jelly mound with two tiny dark curious eyes, a bright dew-drop glint and a small sprouting leaf on top; outer silhouette about 20x14 pixels. Six genuinely different coherent squash/stretch hopping poses: rounded rest, flatten anticipation, stretch up, rounded airborne, soften landing, recover. Keep its friendly wild-monster identity and leaf consistent.

sources.name: title-logo
sources.prompt:
Use case: logo-brand
Asset type: actual transparent pixel-art title wordmark asset for the original 2D sandbox game Starsoil, NOT a screen mockup.
Primary request: A beautiful, carefully crafted horizontal game title logo reading exactly "STARSOIL". Original pixel-art adventure lettering, reminiscent of the handcrafted charm of classic pixel sandbox games such as Terraria but with original letterforms and Starsoil's own crystal-and-soil identity.
Composition: Wide horizontal wordmark with a small integrated faceted cyan star-crystal rising from a tiny moss-covered earth island at the left, followed by the eight large, clearly legible capital letters S T A R S O I L. The lettering has pale parchment and warm golden stone faces, aged copper undersides, a 1-pixel midnight outline and restrained turquoise crystal accents. A few tiny green shoots grow from the first and last letters; do not obscure their silhouettes.
Pixel specification: This must survive reduction to a native 224x48 pixel transparent sprite. Build the art as chunky intentional pixels at that native size: approximately 22-28 pixel-tall letter faces, consistent baseline, 2-3 pixel stems, clean steps, generous counters. The full asset must fit a 224x48 logical canvas including the crystal emblem and its highlights. Render enlarged for delivery, preferably 1536x512. Keep the entire silhouette inside the canvas with transparent padding. No small painterly detail.
Palette: about 24-48 flat colors, ink navy, dark slate, warm copper, creamy light gold and cool cyan. Solid crisp square pixel clusters, no smooth gradients, no semitransparent glow.
Text verbatim: STARSOIL
Avoid: Chinese subtitle, other words, labels, borders, mockup UI, background scenery, drop shadow outside the tight silhouette, Terraria's logo letters, antialiasing, bevelled vector text, glossy 3D rendering, excessive ornaments. Genuine transparent background.
